questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and keep drivers safe. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find and understand the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit in the rear with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front with an airbag.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
Is a good habit and is required by law.
Is necessary only during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because impatient drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Keep the car straight and slowly ease off the gas pedal to slow down.
Keep your current speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slowly ease off the gas pedal to slow down.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Ease your foot off the gas and do not brake until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and pull to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It affects neither driving skills nor judgment.
It hurts driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms the skills needed for safe driving. It slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, affects your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal the lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver who continues without stopping.
One driver who waves others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign means a steep hill is coming. You should slow down and be prepared.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a crash, move your vehicle off the road and stop if you can. Check if anyone is hurt. Call 911 if needed. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone is killed, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: When driving, when are you allowed to text?

options.text: At red lights.
Never.
By using voice-to-text.
If you don't look at the phone.

questions.explanation: You cannot use a phone to write, send, or read messages while driving. This includes texts, emails, instant messages, and accessing the Internet.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which situations?

options.text: At a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a police officer orders you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both effects become stronger.
Nothing happens.
Both effects become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect becomes weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug makes both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
A person is directing traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person is directing traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign means a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes: signal in the direction you want to go, check your rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and make sure no one is entering the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about bad weather driving is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On highways, you must stay alert and react quickly to hazards. Avoid looking at one thing for too long to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When directed to do so by a flagger.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger or stop sign directs you to stop. Also stop when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Before starting your car, what should you check?

options.text: Only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions make it harder to focus on driving. Worry, anger, fear, and sadness reduce your ability to drive safely. Wait to drive if you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.
